tool.help:
**GotohScan** is a search tool that finds shorter sequences (usually genes) in large database sequences (chromosomes, genomes, ...) by computing all semi-global alignments. Thus, the query sequence is never truncated or split into subsequences, but always mapped to the database over its complete length. The alignment is computed via the Gotoh-alignment algorithm using affine gap costs.
-----
# Inputs
- **Input Database** — the (typically large) sequences to search in, FASTA format. - **Input Query** — the shorter sequence(s) to locate, FASTA format. The query is never truncated or split, and is always aligned over its complete length. - **Database is split into subsequences of size** — the database is processed in chunks of this many nucleotides (default: 10000). This only affects memory usage and progress reporting, not which hits are found. - **E-value** — report only hits with an E-value below this threshold. Should be smaller than 10 (default: 1e-3). - **Percent identity of aligned sequences** — report only hits with at least this percent identity, in the range [0.0, 100.00]. - **Print score distribution data for each query to a file** — writes the score distribution per query (xmgrace `.agr` format) next to the result. - **Output Format** — see below.
# Output formats
| Value | Format | | ----- | ------ | | 0 | BLAST tabular output | | 1 | BLAST tabular output + aligned sequences | | 2 | FASTA — hit sequence only, without gaps | | 3 | MAF — note: header is truncated to 30 characters | | 4 | BED + aligned sequences | | 5 | GFF + aligned sequences |
